pr_body:
pam_nologin looks for /etc/nologin and /run/nologin. user-sessions creates (and removes) /run/nologin, but also removes /etc/nologin. (This behaviour is unchanged since the introduction of the binary in e92787416c691c3f34f47349e5eae3fa68eae856.)

/etc/nologin can be used by administrator to disable user logins, e.g. for extended maintanance. There is no good reason for us to remove it. The goal of user-sessions is not to allow users to log in at any cost, but just to prohibit logins during shutdown and startup. Let's leave /etc/nologin for the administrator.

The makes the code match the man page.

Fixes #26965.
pr_comments: This is technically a compat break, no? In theory someone could be relying on this behavior, eg create the file, so some stuff and then just reboot knowing it will be gone. Sounds be fine to do, but should be mentioned at the top of the news? (Can be done separately)
Yes, I expect this to be mentioned in NEWS.

Hmmm, I read the your comments in the issue, and I don't grok what we're supposed to discuss in relation to this patch. You mention three things: merging the source of messages for `nologin` and `pam_nologin`, other tools looking at `/run/nologin`, and changing `/var/run/` to `/run/` in one more place in util-linux. We already only create `/run/nologin`, so we tools that don't look at that file (possibly via symlink) wouldn't work anyway. And the other proposed changes are irrelevant.

/me looks for `needs-discussion-about-needs-discussion`.

the "needs-discussion" I just added because I only did some initial research, and i don't wanted this to be hurried in before we now all the facts.

i mean, as it stands now the original issue should probably be addressed by just using /etc/nologin.txt, no?

> i mean, as it stands now the original issue should probably be addressed by just using /etc/nologin.txt, no?

No, `/etc/nologin.txt` used by `/sbin/nologin`. It has no relevance for `pam_nologin`, right now. And as I wrote in https://github.com/systemd/systemd/issues/26965#issuecomment-1484760390, I don't think it should.
also, please update the commit message with a brief mention that we stop supporting historical systems with this that do not know /run/nologin in PAM.

hmm, glibc's /usr/include/paths.h  defines _PATH_NOLOGIN pointing to /etc/nologin btw.

We might want add a brief comment about the fact we ignore that too somewhere. I think that macro is mostly a historical BSD thing. Deserves to be ignored, but a brief comment should be added nonetheless.
urks. shadow defines the /etc/nologin too, via NOLOGINS_FILE in login.defs. No idea what for. I hope we won#t lose compat with that.
so shadow apparently supports non-PAM builds where it checks that file itself. I guess we don't have to support that. so let's ignore that cruft.
looks good. but would prefer if such things that (even if only remotely) look like compat breakages would be committed along with their NEWS entry already.
I'll write the NEWS entry when the time comes. I want to look over the commit list anyway, and it's just less work to write everything at once.

issue_context.title: systemd-user-sessions deletes /etc/nologin
issue_context.body:
### systemd version the issue has been seen with

252

### Used distribution

Debian

### Linux kernel version used

_No response_

### CPU architectures issue was seen on

None

### Component

systemd

### Expected behaviour you didn't see

_No response_

### Unexpected behaviour you saw

We use pam_nologin to deny user access to systems whilst we work on them. Recently, whilst doing maintenance on a server, I put a helpful message into /etc/nologin. After a reboot, I was surprised to discover that this file had been deleted by something which led to users gaining access before we were ready.

Using the Linux auditd I tracked down the file deletion to systemd-user-sessions.service. Reading the man page for that service, it only mentions using the /run/nologin file.  Checking the source code for src/user-sessions/user-sessions.c though I see in the start method:

                r = unlink_or_warn("/run/nologin");
                k = unlink_or_warn("/etc/nologin");

There doesn't seem to be any good reason given for this service to also delete the file in /etc.  This leaves me with no easy way to set my own nologin file that will be preserved over a reboot. I realise that I could just remove the service completely but this doesn't seem like appropriate behaviour, I'm sure it will surprise other sysadmins who expect to be able to rely on pam_nologin to keep systems secure.

comments:
The code was like this since its introduction in e92787416c691c3f34f47349e5eae3fa68eae856. pam_nologin looks for both files.

I think it would be reasonable to adjust the code to match the docs. We should only delete the file that we create ourselves. I don't think there's a good reason to touch `/etc`, this is admin territory.

/run/nologin was our invention, we asked for the file to be moved from /etc/ to /run/ and it was. Long ago. We still manage both files because we wanted compat with the old PAM. Before dropping the old file we should verifiy support for /run/nologin is well enough supported elsewhere and for long enough, and maybe document the minimal version of PAM (and login?) that we then require to work correctly.

/etc/nologin was never an admin thing on sysv but a system thing. We can turn it into an admin thing now though I guess, but this is a change of semantics.
man-pages package still only mentions /etc/nologin, and no /run/nologin. Needs further investigation whether we really can drop this.

So util-linux `nologin` tool actually shows `/etc/nologin.txt`, and neither `/etc/nologin` nor `/run/nologin`...

This seems quite confusing.

PAM added support for `/var/run/nologin` in e9e593f6ddeaf975b7fe8446d184e6bc387d450b btw, which is from 2010.

I think it probably would make sense to ask them to update this to actually reference `/run/nologin` since `/var/run/` is a symlink to `/run/` anyway, and the indirection just means the file can be accessed during late boot only.

hey @karelzak what's the story with util-linux reading `/etc/nologin.txt`? why different from pam_nologin?

hey, @ldv-alt can we change pam_nologin to check `/run/nologin` instead of `/var/run/nologin`?

i.e. can we maybe agree that every tool checks `/etc/nologin` first, and then `/run/nologin` as fallback? 

And then systemd would only bother with `/run/nologin`, and nothing else anymore.

> So util-linux `nologin` tool actually shows `/etc/nologin.txt`, and neither `/etc/nologin` nor `/run/nologin`...

`nologin` is a per-user mechanism, generally unrelated to `pam_nologin`. It is reasonable that they use the different files for the message, though the naming could be a bit clearer.
hmm, indeed /etc/nologin.txt and /etc/nologin are indeed different things. I wished the man pages would clear this up. Man this is confusing.

The man page for pam_nologin (at least on Debian and Ubuntu) is fairly
clear:

      pam_nologin is a PAM module that prevents users from logging into the
       system when /var/run/nologin or /etc/nologin exists. The contents of
       the file are displayed to the user.

I think that's ideal behaviour, it allows for systemd stuff to happen with
/var/run/nologin and for the admin to also express a preference with the
file in /etc/nologin.

nologin(1) from util-linux replaces shell in /etc/passwd. It always refuses login to the system, and the optional file /etc/nologin.txt is just a message for users, nothing else.

PAM uses  /var/run/nologin or /etc/nologin to control the module behavior.  See man nologin(1), NOTES section.

It means the purpose of the files is completely different.  

(Maybe /etc/nologin.mesg would be a better name for the file, but it's probably too late to change it.)
